summary: The bill requires private health plans, Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, and VA health care to cover supplemental breast cancer screenings such as ultrasounds, MRIs, and molecular imaging without cost-sharing for people at higher risk or with dense breasts, using National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines to set eligibility and frequency, effective 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates expanded coverage without cost-sharing for breast cancer screenings under Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, and VA health programs. This directly increases federal outlays for these services starting in 2026, expanding government healthcare spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.

The bill requires no-cost-sharing coverage for additional breast screenings across private insurance (group/individual plans), Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, and VA. It imposes mandates on private plans and expands benefits in public programs, pushing toward broader mandated coverage rather than purely market-based approaches.
The bill has no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no provisions related to immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant protections.
The bill has no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill requires TRICARE (military health coverage) to provide no-cost-sharing breast screenings for eligible individuals, creating a minor increase in military healthcare spending.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy.
The bill expands Medicaid benefits by requiring coverage of additional breast screenings without cost-sharing for at-risk individuals, directly expanding a key safety-net program.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no provisions related to drugs, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill has no provisions related to policing, sentencing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
By increasing federal spending on Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, and VA programs, the bill contributes to higher deficits rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
The bill has no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill has no provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
The bill has no provisions related to voting access, elections, or voter ID.
The bill has no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or tech oversight.
The bill has no provisions related to unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The bill has no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
